initial_state.data: FiniteBatchInstance contains a duplicate-free finite domain, fixed ordered arbitrary source functions, fixed claims with equal lane count, degree bound, concrete scalarRSResidual weights, and positive integer agreement threshold.
initial_state.good: A single degree-bounded polynomial tuple jointly agrees with all source lanes on at least threshold domain points, and every candidate's concrete weighted coefficient functional equals its fixed lane claim.
initial_state.doomed: No such tuple exists. This is an existential candidate-language predicate, not a premise that the source is honest or already polynomial.

post_alpha_state.good: There exists one polynomial of the required degree agreeing with the deterministic virtual batched oracle on threshold points and satisfying the alpha-power-batched residual claim.
post_alpha_state.critical_obligation: From initial doomed state, bound the number of alpha values whose post-alpha state is good. FiniteVirtualBatchRBRObligation defines precisely this implication; the file does NOT prove it or postulate it as an axiom.
post_alpha_state.why_existing_roots_do_not_suffice: The candidate polynomial may depend on alpha. A root bound for one fixed false claim vector does not bound the union over an uncontrolled adaptive candidate family. Source-oracle authentication fixes oracle values, not decoded candidate polynomials.

proved_component.statement: For any fixed finite family of T candidate tuples, each yielding an L-element claim vector differing from the target, at most T*(L-1) distinct alpha samples can make any candidate's batched claim match. Actual polynomial tuples use scalarRSResidual, not an abstract honest-value oracle.
proved_component.scope: No candidate existence, list bound or proximity result is assumed or manufactured. Family members may switch with alpha; the finite union count is proved explicitly.
proved_component.needed_to_use_it: A complete small family fixed before alpha, covering every successful post-alpha candidate through the relevant batching relation, and a proof that each family's tuple violates at least one fixed claim. These are not available from the scalar algebra modules.
proved_component.enumeration_warning: Enumerating all degree<D tuples gives roughly |K|^(D*L) possibilities; multiplying by L-1 yields no useful security. Enumerating separate per-lane nearby candidates also does not establish that every nearby batched candidate decomposes into one of those tuples.

mandatory_external_math.revision: Author-uploaded June13,2026 text; PDF bytes not archived, as documented in custom-fold-security-theorem-review.json
mandatory_external_math.initial_batching: Section5.1 Lemma1 uses constrained correlated agreement. Theorems2/3 give linear-subspace and weighted forms. Their common agreement conclusion is the substantive missing theorem for arbitrary virtual source oracles.
mandatory_external_math.later_folds: Section6.1 Lemma4 invokes Theorem4 for a degree-two challenge-dependent residual constraint. Weighted consistency measures and their denominator bounds must be represented explicitly; unweighted initial batching alone cannot establish the full RBR invariant.
mandatory_external_math.regime: The source states proved bounds at theta=1-sqrt(rho)*(1+1/(2m)), m>=3, and discusses unique-decoding specialization. This is not permission to import an unverified numerical formula or claim our implementation already matches the theorem.
